label: paragraph_title
text: LOCARNO SUCCESS

label: text
text: The text is issued of the Locarno Protocol and Mutual Guarantee Treaty: also of the Arbitration Conventions and agreements already mentioned, which latter are respectively in identical terms' mutatis quotidis.

label: text
text: The Delegates declare their firm conviction that the operation of all instruments will contribute greatly to bring about a moral relaxation of the tension between nations and help powerfully towards a solution of the many political and economic problems, in accordance with national interests and sentiments, and hasten disarmament as provided by article 8 of the League in which they undegetake sincerely to co-operate and seek regulation in general agreement.

label: text
text: The central feature of the work of the Loewno Confidence is the Security Pact guaranteeing the inviolability of the German and Belgian and German and French frontiers.

label: text
text: CENTRAL FENTURG

label: text
text: The parties definitely pledge themselves not to begin war against each other, and only where a unanimous decision of the League Council Assembly calls for such action can either party initiate bellicose measures.

label: text
text: The article of the Treaty which particularly affects Britain contains guarantees that she has a contracting party will support Germany, if France and Belgium attack her or vice versa. One article of the Treaty makes it clear that it does not in the slightest undermine the authority of the League, but is intended to strengthen it.

label: text
text: The Treaty is to be regarded as having outlived its purpose when the League has grown in strength and is able to provide the guarantee of security contaminated in the Locarno Treaty.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUPPORT FOR LEAG

label: text
text: The Treaty's main points otherwise are as already cabled, except in regard to Article 16 of the Covenant in which it is stated: a draft collective note will be presented to Germany, propounding as an interpretation thereof that obligations mean that each League member is bound to co-operate to support the Covenant and resist any act of aggression to an extent compatible with the military situation and geographical position.

label: text
text: The subordinate, arbitration treaties to which Poland and Czecho-Slovakia and parties, provide that if Germany fails to observe the provisions of the Arbitration Treaty and couples failure with a resort to war, the parties will reciprocally help each other.

label: paragraph_title
text: A DECISIVE POINT.

label: paragraph_title
text: Paris, October 19

label: text
text: Mr. Austen Chamberlain, in an interview, given to English French and American journalists, said he was convinced that the "Locarno" agreements had reached a decisive point in the history for the peace of Europe and the world. He recalled that the initiative emanated from Germany "in act of high courage and great wisdom:"

label: text
text: He especially paid a tribute to Herr Stresemann and Dr. Luther. He declared that when he came to the Foreign Office the ruling spirit in Europe was the war spirit. He believed that if it had lasted a few years longer it would be too late to remedy eventually and would lead to a catastrophe, possibly more disastrous to the world than the Great War.

label: text
text: MEANING OF THE VICTORY.

label: text
text: The Locarno agreements had been reached because his conferees had met on a footing of equality, each with a full sense of responsibility and desiring peace with all his might.

label: text
text: At Locarno, however, the Allies and Germany found accommodation based on the Anglo-French entente on which a reconciliation with Germany was possible.

label: text
text: There had been no victory over any country—the only victory was a victory for peace over war.

label: doc_title
text: LONDON REUNION.

label: text
text: On the invitation of Commissioner and Mrs. Li, R. Halifax there was a huge muster of ex-Hongkongites and Hongkong residents on leave as well as many Exhibition Commissioners and officials and friends at the Hongkong Pavilion on Tuesday, September 22, to mark the termination of Hongkong's successful participation in the great Empire Exhibition at Wembley. The gathering took the form of an "at home," Mr. and Mrs. Halifax receiving their many guests under cover of that popular feature the Chinese Restaurant, where refreshments were served. The response to the invitation was an almost unanimous one. There being close on five hundred acceptances, exclusive of the general list, and it seemed that only distance (several of those envied being in Scotland and elsewhere remote) prevented the gathering from being a complete reunion of all who have been associated with Hongkong and who are now in this country. The turnout was very, gratifying, the more especially as the weather was so in-element, to the Commissioner, and those participating with him in the work at Wembley. As was the case last year, the Hongkong section, owing to the advent of the cold vailler and the long journey before the returning Chinese, will be closed down earlier than the main part of the Exhibition, good The gathering on September 22, give all who attended a last opportunity of seeing the section in full operation. It was in every way an enjoyable and most successful function.

label: paragraph_title
text: DRUG TRAFFIC

label: text
text: SCOTLAND YARD'S TASK:

label: text
text: London, Sept. 20

label: text
text: Brilliant Chang; the dope king, has been lost to London, but he has been deposed only that another Moriarty of the drug traffic can rule in his place.

label: text
text: Scotland Yard is now faced with a recrudescence in the business of selling "snow," and behind it is a sinister figure who is well-known to the police, but who has so carefully covered his tracks that it is as yet impossible for the police to lay hands on him.

label: text
text: To aid this man are negroes, crooks, and light women of the dance clubs. Yet none of them knows the master.

label: text
text: Following the deportation of Brilliant Chang, who, for some

label: text
text: behind the traffic, it was hoped that the organisation which was responsible for the distribution had had its wings clipped, but Scotland Yard had not to wait long for proof that the traffic had re-opened.

label: text
text: There was no doubt that following the deportation of Brilliant Chang his many associates, bereft of his leadership, and nervous about police activities, decided on a "close" season. They frequented their usual haunts but were afraid to attempt any selling of the drugs at their disposal. This caution has now gone; and the drug traffic is again assuming a serious aspect.

label: paragraph_title
text: A New "Genius:"

label: text
text: Inspector Leach, who has a special squad of detectives at his disposal, is concentrating his attention on the dope traffic. There is no doubt that the place left vacant by Brilliant Chang has been filled by a man of equal organising genius and possessed of such a dominant personality that he has been able to put courage into the men and women who once worked under the banner of Chang, and they are again at their work of distributing drugs in the West End, but they are working with extreme caution.

label: text
text: The new master of the dope traffic is making use of the large number of negroes who live in the Tottenham Court Road district and who frequent public-houses in the notorious Seven Dials districts.

label: text
text: It is known that comparatively large quantities of cocaine and heroin are being smuggled into England at various ports and supplies are transported to London by agents who have motor-cars at their disposal.

label: text
text: The master of the dope traffic lives in the Hampstead district. He has a small business in the City and has so organised the traffic in drugs that he never actually sees the cocaine which his agents distribute. He is known only to a small number of men which take the responsibility of supplying men and women who frequent the West End with their deadly wares. Negroes who, in turn, use nightclub women and others for the actual sale of packets of "snow" are in total ignorance of the "master," except that they know he exists.

label: text
text: His lieutenants, who are crooks with “records”—behind them, have been chosen for that reason. Their employer has them—completely in his power. He could lay information with the police which would lead to the conviction of any of his subordinates. Apart from that he sees to it that his subordinates are well paid. Thus he has every reason to expect and to enforce loyalty from his followers.

label: text
text: This Moriarty of real life has been under police suspicion for some time, but although detectives have searched his home and his city offices, they have found not a shred of evidence against him. His files of correspondence were gone through thoroughly, and his movements closely watched, but he has covered his tracks so completely that nothing has been found which definitely connects him with the drug' traffic. Yet there is not the slightest doubt in the minds of the police that this man is the successor to Brilliant Chang.

label: paragraph_title
text: WOMAN ADDICTED TO OPIUM.

label: text
text: 42 TAELS IN STOCK.

label: text
text: Before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry, at the Central Magistracy this morning, Ma Pak-mui, widow, of 29B, Kennedy Road, second floor, was charged with possession of 42 taels of illicit opium.

label: text
text: Chief Preventive Officer S. J. Clarke said that on information received by him he visited the house yesterday afternoon and found several lots of prepared opium concealed in flower pots in the sitting room and other unlikely places.

label: text
text: Mr. W. B. Hind, appearing for the defendant, said that the woman was a confirmed opium smoker as His Worship could see for himself. The opium was kept for her own use and hidden so as to keep it away from the children in the house. She had been an inmate of the French Hospital twice, but on each occasion had left before being properly cured. Pleading for leniency Mr. Hind suggested that His Worship make an order for the woman to be sent to the Government Civil Hospital and detained there until she was cured of the habit, as it was a thing that she herself desired.

label: text
text: A fine of $2,500 was imposed, or three months' hard labour in default.

At frequent intervals they leave, and soon afterwards they are in conversation with smartly-dressed girls who are later to be found in the night clubs around Piccadilly.

label: text
text: These girls are actually used to sell cocaine and other drugs in the night clubs and bars. The "Sunday Chronicle" representative was offered "snow" done up in white paper packets from women dancing partners three times during a comparatively short visit to a comparatively unknown night club. In two instances the girls had not the "snow" actually in their possession, but offered to obtain supplies from persons outside the club within five minutes. The other girl had several packets concealed in her stockings.

label: text
text: The terrible thing about this end of the dope traffic is that the majority of these girls are young and appear to be blissfully unaware of the grave risks they run in selling "dope" to casual acquaintances. They obtain their supplies from their negro protectors who, in turn, get the "snow" from a mysterious source somewhere on the outer edge of London.

label: text
text:
Although detectives have been busy during the past week, collecting information and spending hours in observation work, they have far-failed to obtain the information they have been seen. They could have made several minor arrests in connection with the traffic in cocaine, but this would have spread the alarm and they would have got no access to the main source of the supply.
